How to switch characters in GTA 6 and give your partner instructions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1329 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are two playable characters in GTA 6 to switch between – Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.
  • Whether you're playing through one of the main GTA 6 missions or just exploring the wide open world of Leonida, the game is undoubtedly at its best when Jason and Lucia are working together.
  • You aren't able to immediately switch characters in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are two playable characters in GTA 6 to switch between – Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. They are partners in crime, working together to make enough money in Leonida to build a better future. That means that you'll need to engage with both characters to get the most out of your time with the world. Thankfully, Rockstar Games has built in a number of different ways for Jason and Lucia to interact.

Whether you're playing through one of the main GTA 6 missions or just exploring the wide open world of Leonida, the game is undoubtedly at its best when Jason and Lucia are working together. Below I'm going to break down how to switch characters in GTA 6, how to meet up with your partner, and give you some top tips on how to work as a more effective pair when you're engaging in a little crime.

You aren't able to immediately switch characters in GTA 6. The option will become available once you hit a certain milestone in Chapter 2. Once both of the characters are available, hold right on the d-pad and press R1/RB to switch between the characters.

Industry observers note that there are infrequent restrictions to swapping characters in GTA 6. Sometimes your partner will be busy, with a darkened character profile once you hold left on the d-pad indicating that you can't switch right away. Keep checking in though, as they will eventually be available.

Industry observers note that tip: Jason and Lucia will sometimes have their own tasks which require you to switch characters. If you see either a J or an L on the map it means that the mission must be played solo.

Sources indicate that checking in with your partner regularly is a great way to improve your relationship status in GTA 6. There's a couple of ways to do this, but the easiest is to message them through WhatUp – hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle / Y if there is a blue icon about a character's profile picture, or press up on the d-pad and navigate to the relevant app in the GTA 6 phone menu.

Recent findings suggest that tip: When Jason and Lucia are together, you can use L2/LT to focus on your partner. This will prompt conversations, and give you the opportunity to share items you are holding like food and drink.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Sources indicate that meeting up with your partner is essential throughout GTA 6. The easiest way to reach out is to hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle/Y. Alternatively, you can also navigate to the Contacts app on your phone and call your partner. This will prompt them to drive to where you're right now situated on the GTA 6 map; if you have a destination set, your partner will meet you there.

Tip: If you spend a full day together, look for visual and audio cues that it's time to head home together and get in some much needed rest. A little heart icon will appear around your residence on the map, while sometimes your partner will raise it as an idea in casual conversation.

Recent findings suggest that you don't always need to do the heavy lifting on driving. If you are close to your personal vehicle, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask your partner to drive. Once you're in the passenger seat, open up the map and set a destination, and they will start making their way there.

It has been revealed that the AI pathfinding is solid when your partner is at the wheel, but you can hold Right on the d-pad to issue them instructions to speed up and slow down. You can also use this functionality to ask your partner to split up and take the vehicle with them –a great way of lowering your wanted level in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that tip: If you're at the wheel while being chased by the cops, you can switch characters to take control of the passenger. Just remember that incapacitating police vehicles (even non-lethally) will contribute to a Hardened Criminal Profile in GTA 6.

Whether you're sticking up a local convenience store for petty cash or launching an assault on a bank for a major pay day, you can undertake robberies both solo and as a pair. If you go into the map and hover over the icon of the location you're planning to hit, it'll denote the security – if it's medium to high, you'll want to consider bringing your partner along for the ride.

Before starting a robbery, hold Right on the d-pad to open up some new options for your eventual escape from the location. You can ask your partner to wait in the car while you go inside, helping to save some precious seconds before the cops show up.

Once a robbery is in-progress, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask them to come in from the car to provide backup. Using this method is also a great way to hand over one of your weapons if they need it; each character can only hold two stash bags filled with ill-gotten gains at any one time, but you can also throw these over to your partner to carry.

Industry observers note that tip: Committing a robbery is a fairly intuitive process. If you directly threaten guards or cashiers, this will prompt your partner to support you and hold a weapon on them while you move through a building.

Sources indicate that once you're together, it is possible to have your partner leave for whatever reason. Hold Right on the d-pad to get the option to split up from your partner, leaving you solo with the character you're in primary control of. This can be done at any point while you're exploring the world, but there may be restrictions in certain missions.

If you've got the cops chasing you through the streets, you do have the option to split up. There's two benefits of this: the first is that they can split away from you and distract the cops, reducing some of the heat on you and removing one of the conditions to the GTA 6 Wanted Level you're trying to outrun. The second is that they can also head off and use one of the fences to sell any stolen goods that they have on them without you needing to be there – although, word of warning, the price you'll get for the score may be reduced.

According to recent reports, tip: If you ask a partner to split off from you after a robbery, keep an eye out for a message from them on WhatUp. They will usually ask if they should sell the score or come meet back up with you, and ignoring these messages will have a negative impact on your relationship.

#40205. Tech Report: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1066 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Tech giant of Heroes provides.

Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

According to recent reports, just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

Sources indicate that as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Recent findings suggest that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell says. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

Recent findings suggest that relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Manufacturer of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent revision is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell states foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very swiftly.".

Recent findings suggest that I ask if it was always the blueprint to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had looks to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a major part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Manufacturer of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Organization of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that cost of Hope is the substantial news; a latest add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release.
  • First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Industry observers note that cost of Hope is the substantial news; a latest add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

Industry observers note that the story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

According to recent reports, GSC Game World indicates Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two latest regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

Sources indicate that the developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (340 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that 8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has unveiled the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary.
  • Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers.
  • Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that 8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has unveiled the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's right now scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026.

Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99, it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.

Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too). The pad also features single-rotor rumble to replicate the feel of the original, while a newly introduced 'ZL' button – which also features on the official Nintendo GameCube pad for Switch 2 – has been designed to be symmetrical to the 'Z' button on the right.

While we do have a dedicated capture button, there unfortunately doesn't appear to be a 'C' button for chat purposes. It's also not clear at this stage whether the GC controller will have wake-up support for Switch 2, but 8BitDo has generally been pretty good at including this, even if it's not necessarily supported immediately at launch.

Here's an official list of features from 8BitDo:.

- Classic GC design and iconic button layout - TMR joysticks with octagonal gates - Hall Effect linear triggers - Single-rotor rumble - Symmetrical Z and ZL bumpers - Capture button for screenshots and recording - Turbo function - Support for multiple simultaneous gamepad connections.

Finally, it's worth noting that if you purchase the 8BitDo Retro Receiver for GC, you can use the new controller – or indeed the official GameCube pad – with original hardware.

A Morgan Revolver variant for both Jason and Lucia, including palm-tree etched grips, engravings, and a scope.

This speedboat with a pink and blue palm tree motif comes with an explosive-laden weapons crate.

This signature 90s red and white sports car comes with a retro futuristic livery.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far.
  • Recent findings suggest that there's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer.
  • The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far. It's an incredible racing title that even surpasses the original Star Wars Episode 1 Racer in my view, and I've had so much fun with the campaign and online multiplayer.

Recent findings suggest that there's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer. With that in mind, the development team have found a way to implement it in a new patch.

The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027. Alongside it will be a new mode called Free Play, which is where you'll be able to freely choose your vehicle, character, planet and race track.

"We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.".

It has been revealed that it seems Free Play is the only place where you'll be able to access local split-screen multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer, but that's no surprise considering how solo-focused the main campaign is. They'd literally have to rewrite massive portions of the campaign if they were going to implement split-screen into it.

Anyway, this is just an amazing bonus on top of an already amazing game, and I encourage you to check it out if you enjoy a title like Burnout 3: Takedown - it's fast-paced and frantic, has the same kind of takedown system that you'll remember from that game, and the roguelite campaign is really well designed (online is great fun as well).

If you've played it, let us know what you think of the game in the poll down below!

Excited for local multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer? Tell us in the comments section.

Latest Update: Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.
  • You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics.
  • I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

Sources indicate that my computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

According to recent reports, I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

In a recent development, I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is introduced over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

It has been revealed that I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

Industry observers note that the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

In a recent development, the main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

According to recent reports, still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Industry observers note that casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

For the first time in 12 years — since all the way back in 2014 — there is no Sony-published PlayStation title amongst The Game Awards' Game of the Year nominees.

In that time, Sony has won three Game of the Year awards at Geoff's annual show, making it the most successful publisher in the event's history.

But its over-a-decade streak of nominations will finally come to an end here in 2026, as none of its releases from this year have made the cut.

That includes God of War: Sons of Sparta, Marathon, MLB The Show 26, Saros, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, and Marvel's Wolverine.

In particular, Saros and Marvel Tokon got really strong reviews, but given just how stacked this year's competition is, it's no real surprise to see these relatively niche titles be left in the cold.

At the start of the year, many would have probably predicted that Wolverine would be in the mix — but a lukewarm critical reception has ultimately sealed its fate.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some significant news about the next major enhancement. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of newly introduced content, including a significant expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this fresh patch, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

Industry observers note that if you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only latest character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her major gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

In a recent development, linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

It has been revealed that this patch will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no upcoming characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other upcoming arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Can you replay missions in GTA 6?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that want to know something a little surprising about this long-awaited trip to Leonida?
  • With over 90 main story missions in GTA 6, some of which are an absolute riot of a time while others feature pretty substantial branching paths that help shape your GTA 6 Criminal Profile system, it's no surprise that many of you are wondering how to replay your favorite moments from the campaign.
  • It has been revealed that sadly, after playing the game for over 100 hours for my GTA 6 review, I can confirm that there's simply no option to do so.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that want to know something a little surprising about this long-awaited trip to Leonida? Rockstar hasn't put any options in the game to replay missions in GTA 6. That's right, there is no mission replay and it's unlikely that it'll be added in later either.

With over 90 main story missions in GTA 6, some of which are an absolute riot of a time while others feature pretty substantial branching paths that help shape your GTA 6 Criminal Profile system, it's no surprise that many of you are wondering how to replay your favorite moments from the campaign.

It has been revealed that sadly, after playing the game for over 100 hours for my GTA 6 review, I can confirm that there's simply no option to do so. It kind of makes sense when you think about it.

GTA 5 did let you replay missions easy enough, but that was a way to let you back into key moments to try and complete skill challenges – Rockstar has since moved all of the GTA 6 challenges into its own spot in the progress menu. They are now far broader in scope, and primarily used to unlock GTA 6 cheats once you've wrapped up the story.

According to recent reports, if you're worried about missing anything or wanting to play key moments from a chapter again, I would recommend that you learn the ins and outs of the GTA 6 save system – this lets you keep and load back into 15 different sessions. Otherwise, you'd have to start a whole fresh game just to replay a mission in GTA 6!

Industry observers note that the new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

In a recent development, alongside the major fresh Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

It has been revealed that if you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the newly introduced Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

Sources indicate that the Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

Industry observers note that after you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an notable part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

Considering we're just a few days away from the release of GTA 6 on November 19th, we're bound to start getting reviews at some point between now and launch, and it'll be fascinating to see what the critics think of it!

This is a series that has consistently dominated on Metacritic over the years - a website that takes loads of professional reviews and creates an average score based around them. Grand Theft Auto V has a 97 average rating on there, for example, while GTA 4 goes even higher with a 98 rating.

In fact, every mainline release since GTA 3 (not including stuff like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories) has reached at least a 95 on the platform. To put that into context, the best-rated Xbox Series X game of the year on Metacritic right now is Hades 2, and that game has a 95 average rating.

It has been revealed that if we're going off history alone, GTA 6 has every chance of becoming the highest-reviewed game of 2026 on Xbox and PS5. The question is whether it'll manage to hit those highs once again, or whether it'll struggle to meet the hype.

Let's not forget there's never been a wait like this for a GTA game before, and while absence definitely does make the heart grow fonder, it also creates a sense of expectation that's extremely difficult to live up to.

We'll have to wait and see what happens! You'll find a review roundup on Pure Xbox ASAP, and it seems the smart bet is at least a 95 rating on Metacritic, although that's much easier mentioned than achieved.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding newly introduced content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 revision.
  • Industry observers note that "The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 update to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are new quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

In a recent development, "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding newly introduced content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 revision. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

Industry observers note that "The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

As laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

In a recent development, more clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A fresh opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

"All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

In a recent development, you can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's enhancement.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a new playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6's criminal profiles (plural, because Jason and Lucia each have their own criminal profile) tracks how you treat other people in the world, reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. How violent you are, how lethal you are in your encounters, and how you treat people and animals in the world will all affect your rating.

There are five levels for Jason and Lucia's criminal profile, represented by "face with horns" emoji-style icons that are shown on your screen:.

Industry observers note that your criminal profile is almost entirely dependent on how often you kill people. Try to incapacitate enemies, or wound them instead of killing them, and don't kill too many police or civilians, and you'll wind up with a Professional or Hardened profile. If you're violent for no reason, kill a lot of cops and civilians, and kill pets or defenseless animals, you'll gain a Violent, Psycho, or Irredeemable profile.

Here are the behaviors that will grant you each of the criminal profiles, and the bonuses that come with them:.

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (bullet-time).

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (same as Professional).

Bonus: Headshots will increase your focus meter.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Bonus: Headhosts will increase your focus meter, but you will be unable to surrender to cops.

It has been revealed that if you're a Psycho for too long, you'll gain the Irredeemable profile. While you can move up and down between the other four profiles during the game, once you have an Irredeemable criminal profile, it's permanent.

Sources indicate that according to Rockstar, "being irredeemable will have a lasting impact on Jason and Lucia," though we don't yet know what that means. We'll patch this guide when we find out.

For my playthrough of the main story, I typically kept both Jason and Lucia in the Professional range, which is the profile I finished the main story with, though I did occasionally drop both of them down to Hardened.

I did this by (mostly) trying to be non-lethal in my encounters, using focus to aim for my enemies' knees and elbows during shootouts. I still killed a whole mess of people in my playthrough.

Here are my endgame stats that achieved me a Professional criminal profile:.

*A note on that animal total: I did a little bit of hunting, and I once ran over a cat (by accident!). But most of those animal kills, I suspect, are birds, which have some of the worst AI I've ever seen in a game. They do not get out of the way of cars, trucks, boats, planes, helicopters, ATVs, scooters, and even bicycles. You are going to run over a lot of birds. Sorry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 features a manual save system. You can do this at practically any time, giving you the freedom to create your checkpoint in Leonida and come back to the game at a later date. Given that there are close to 100 GTA 6 Missions, this is going to come in very handy – particularly as there is no way to replay missions in GTA 6.

However, there is one significant limitation. There are only 15 manual save slots in GTA 6. It would be wise to keep one at the beginning and end of each major chapter, giving you the freedom to jump around if you want or need to. As for how you save in GTA 6, you just need to follow these easy steps:.

You can overwrite and load into any of these save slots in GTA 6. It's also worth mentioning that there is a single, secret 16th slot that is reserved for an auto-save which triggers after missions, if you're wasted, busted, or have some sort of major encounter in the open world.

The save system will also disable if you activate any GTA 6 cheats, forcing you to quit out of the game and reload a save that wasn't revelling in pure chaos.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 should let you save at any time, but if you're encountering a problem there's likely a good reason for it. You can't save in GTA 6 while you're on a mission. Instead you'll need to rely on the auto-save functionality, although you can restart missions from the beginning or from checkpoints by pressing the start button.

Recent findings suggest that if you're in free-roam and you can't save in GTA 6, it may be because Jason or Lucia just finished a phone conversation or objective. Try leaving the building or vehicle that you're in and try again.

In a recent development, there is no in-game option to quit out of GTA 6. If you want to end a session, you'll need to head back to the home screen of your PS5 or Xbox Series X and close the application manually. If you do this, just remember to save first – otherwise you'll be relying on the last auto-save GTA 6 made.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC prepares. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

Industry observers note that 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That said, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game currently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that as you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

Rounding out the expansion are latest enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an patch alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

As much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

December is often a very quiet month for fresh game releases, and that's particularly going to be the case in 2026 due to GTA 6's arrival and the desire from publishers to get as far away from it as possible, but we've still got the likes of Rayman Legends Retold and Stage Tour to look forward to, along with a couple of first-party Xbox expansions.

In terms of first-party stuff, Xbox is initially releasing a paid DLC pack for Minecraft Dungeons 2 on December 1st called The Humblers Awaken. This DLC is included with the Deluxe Edition of the game if you bought it, and it'll be available separately as well.

You can expect "new quests, unexplored environments, colorful cosmetics, and an expanded arsenal of powerful gear" in The Humblers Awaken, while base game players will also be treated to a free revision on the same day, adding in new challenges, weapons and armour.

Recent findings suggest that then, just a day later, Xbox and Obsidian are releasing a first expansion for The Outer Worlds 2, known as Side Effects Guaranteed. This DLC includes a upcoming narrative story (that'll be concluded in the second part next year), a new region of Elysium Valley to explore, new threats, new perks and an increased level cap.

There's also new weapons, armours, outfits, flaws, a new radio station - you get the picture!

Side Effects Guaranteed will cost $14.99 USD when it arrives on December 2nd, or you'll get it included if you bought either the Premium Edition or Premium Upgrade Edition of The Outer Worlds 2.

Perhaps there's a chance we might get even more from Xbox's first-party studios in December, but as mentioned, it's typically a month where the releases die down. In any case, it's nice to see two expansions on the way very soon!

The Sift is in danger! Something ancient is stirring beneath the ground of the latest dimension – a threat that has slumbered for ages and is now beginning to wake. Gather your trusty allies, venture deep into unexplored reaches, take on the not-so-happy humblers, and confront the foes behind their rude awakening!

Side Effects Guaranteed is the first chapter of a two-part expansion for The Outer Worlds 2. A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation to keep themselves alive, as they’ve been infected with something that causes explosive cell death. The hunt for a cure leads to Elysium Valley, a brand-newly introduced region on Eden.

Excited for either of these Xbox expansions? Tell us down in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today.
  • You can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site.
  • Industry observers note that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have big consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.

You can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site. The organisers have also published an introductory explainer that takes us through the timeline of the Act's gestation, dating back to 2020, and summarises its provisions. If passed, the Act will apply to any tech giant doing business in the EU, not just those based in member states, with individual governments able to impose fines and consumers able to seek financial compensation if they think they've been harmed.

Industry observers note that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text. The Act proposes a number of provisions regarding "unfair" commercial practices, including omission and distortion in advertising and PR communication at large. Amongst other things, it takes aim at "dark patterns" – that is, "visual, auditory and other components" of online interfaces that are designed to manipulate or deceive. The text also forbids personalised advertising and pricing aimed at children, and prohibits influencers from making "direct exhortations to minors to buy products or to persuade their parents or other adults to buy products in commercial communications".

The items that are probably of greatest interest to us smelly gamers are the passages on virtual currencies, "variable reward systems", and addictive design.

It has been revealed that the Act would require game publishers who sell virtual currencies to indicate the real-world monetary value of the currency and anything bought with it. It would also require companies to disable paid-for virtual currencies by default for kids, unless a parent or guardian has given approval.

As for paid-for "variable reward systems", aka "loot boxes", "surprise mechanics", "Schrödinger's Giftbombs" or however publishers may prefer to describe them, the Act would require companies to state the "types" of object they might cough up, together with the probability of obtaining them. It would also oblige publishers to disable paid-for "variable reward systems" for minors, and give everybody an "easily accessible" way to switch them off.

The draft Act outright prohibits "pay-to-progress and pay-to-win mechanisms" for kids. More generally, it suggests further constraints for publishers and developers who "design, organise or operate their digital products in a manner that is intended, or can reasonably be foreseen to encourage compulsive or excessive use". Again, it wants companies to give people options to switch these features off.

That includes "features enabling automatic play of content and uninterrupted content consumption without effective and regular interruption moments that enable deliberation by the consumer on their willingness to consume more content". Also, "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the consumer’s interaction or activity on the service", "features incentivising engagement at regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits", and "features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations," such as nagging prompts.

Industry observers note that if you'd like a more 'expert' account of the Digital Fairness Act - how dare you! I have read several Wikipedia pages - the bespectacled nabobs of GamesIndustry.biz went and got notes from an actual lawyer. All this follows a change in EU rating law last month aimed at safeguarding the weans from predatory habit-forming devices and instruments of financialisation - games with lootboxes are now PEGI 16 by default, while blockchain games are always rated 18. Across the pond, meanwhile, lawsuits are underway in Latest York and Washington against Valve's tolerance of lootboxes on Steam, which the lawyers in question define as illegal gambling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The latest update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The massive inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Recent findings suggest that our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

In a recent development, this is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

In a recent development, keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent upcoming characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

Industry observers note that you may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a newly introduced weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

Sources indicate that it can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Industry observers note that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this enhancement, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

According to recent reports, as part of the same enhancement, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a major expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding latest decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 releases and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans!
  • According to recent reports, black Forest, based in Germany, revealed the move in a press release.
  • "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and declared intends to form a latest "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

According to recent reports, black Forest, based in Germany, revealed the move in a press release. "We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together," co-boss Adrian Goersch mentioned. "Now, we're excited to shape our own future as owners again, to work on an exciting new project with a great team and strong partners behind us.".

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." As of writing, Third Signal's website is just a logo splash which promises something coming soon. To be fair, it does also look to have an email address, plus legal and privacy notices. Black Forest's management team will become a co-owner of the studio group as part of this move, but "continue to collaborate on game development tasks" with THQ Nordic.

Black Forest had been in the embrace since 2017, releasing both 2020's Destroy All Humans! remake and Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed in that time, plus DLC Clone Carnage. Over the years they've also made multiple entries in the Giana Sisters platformer series, survival game Fade to Silence, and 2017's Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back.

That's a right old mix of stuff, but the biggest names in it are all resurrections of series or characters created by other folks back in the day. Pandemic Studios in the case of Destroy All Humans!, Accolade in the case of Bubsy, and Germany organization Time Warp in the case of Giana Sisters. That makes the fact it sounds like this move'll give Black Forest a bit more creative freedom intriguing. Here's hoping that if they do initiative to try and get some more of their own original ideas off the ground, rather than trucking on with a steady diet of remakes and revivals, they manage to stick the landing. It's all fine declaring that a 50 person team can make a top game these days, but that certainly doesn't mean it's in any way easy to pull off.
